capabilities.title: Agent Workspace
capabilities.local_deviation: The sidecar owns local execution and must return structured unavailable authority for secure environment HITL until vault sealing is implemented.
capabilities.judgment_rationale: Current-HEAD implements canonical Queue/Steer run inputs, atomic HITL denial feedback, encrypted secure-env responses, roster and SubAgent control, Activity read receipts, My Work summaries, and scoped Changes. Web, Cloud Desktop, and Local Desktop remain partial until one clean current-HEAD aggregate supplies every required renderer, backend or sidecar, and native Electron evidence channel without the recorded usage, direct-open, or Queue/Steer observation gaps. Chat and new-thread composers now share required V2 catalog composition and the Project Sandbox Upload authority. The former direct chat roster, marketplace, conversation-list and comparison-history calls use existing WorkspaceRoster, PluginMarketplace, WorkspaceConversationCatalog and NewTaskFlow operations while preserving legacy project/workspace/unbound filters and abort signals. Upload acquires a project lease with frozen tenant/project scope, validates Cloud project ownership before reading file bytes, and sends import_file with fixed /workspace/input destination and overwrite true through the existing project-authorized native broker path. Actual buffer size and successful authoritative return path/size must match the captured file metadata. Local upload is a loaded capability that explicitly rejects with local_sandbox_upload_unavailable; no sidecar execute authority is invented. Composer batch cancellation prevents late reads/uploads from dispatching subsequent files or attaching results after context replacement. Source wiring and software checks do not supply the clean aggregate renderer/backend/sidecar/native evidence required above, and do not promote actions, runtime status or native acceptance. The native Cloud request broker applies a narrowly scoped body-size exception for canonical import_file payloads up to 16 MiB of decoded bytes, with exact fields, canonical base64, fixed input destination and overwrite setting; the exception retains normal endpoint authorization, trusted-session loading and observed project-scope enforcement and is not native upload execution evidence. Sandbox capabilities, remote desktop sessions and structured file list/read/download now use a required project-scoped V2 Surface authority. Cloud operations retain project ownership preflight and sandbox/isolated file authority; Local files remain native_workspace/not_applicable and Local remote desktop remains not applicable, without inferred capability promotion. Remote desktop sessions retain their service lease until explicit release or cancellation, while hook context replacement invalidates late completions. Native Cloud binary downloads carry validated file contract version, authority and isolation through the broker response and renderer reconstruction; missing or mismatched authority is rejected instead of synthesizing headers. Bounded path, structured payload, UTF-8 read and 16 MiB download validation remain software contract checks, not native execution or clean aggregate acceptance evidence. Cloud native Kasm iframe authentication remains an identified gap: the backend desktop-session endpoint seeds a scoped HttpOnly cookie, but the vault-bound main-process request uses net.fetch with credentials omit and the broker only returns the descriptor JSON, without installing that cookie into the iframe session. The existing seedProxyAuthCookie path is used by Local terminal startup, where the sidecar endpoint is a no-op and the socket uses explicit authentication protocols; Cloud TerminalSessionV2 uses the native authenticated socket bridge instead. Neither terminal path supplies a reusable Cloud Kasm cookie installer. A ready descriptor therefore does not prove authenticated iframe execution in a clean native profile. A separate security-scoped native batch must implement and verify the cookie or proxy authority without broadly enabling ambient cookies; this batch retains partial status and does not claim Kasm native success. Activity read-state GET, PUT and flush now use the required project-scoped V2 authority with explicit principal/tenant/project/runtime scope, Cloud project ownership preflight and the existing Local authenticated sidecar protocol. Retry storage uses an authority-qualified v2 key and does not infer ownership for old unqualified v1 keys. Successful PUT acknowledges only the submitted receipt snapshot, preserving concurrent new entries and higher revision or later read timestamps. Flush reads pending state and performs GET/CAS PUT under one admitted operation; only a PUT transport failure may enqueue receipts, while aborts, scope failures, HTTP conflicts and contract failures do not become offline success. These composition and retry-integrity changes preserve the existing partial aggregate/native acceptance requirements. The native broker emits the dedicated activity_read_state_transport_unavailable marker only for a delivery failure of the authorized Activity read-state PUT, after trusted-session loading and observed-scope enforcement; preflight, GET, cancellation and HTTP/CAS failures retain their rejection semantics. Retry merges exceeding the 500-entry protocol bound reject before persistence and preserve the previous queue, rather than persisting data that would be discarded on the next read. Run summary and Changes review now extend the existing SessionProjection and SessionRunChanges V2 authorities rather than adding parallel modules. Cloud summary validates tenant, project, conversation and run identity; a missing persisted summary remains a legitimate partial result with null metrics. Cloud Changes performs summary ownership validation and the requested changes read within one session lease, preserving run, session and turn scopes, required turn_id for turn scope, and expected_revision >= 1. Local Changes retains its real run-only sidecar contract with expected_revision >= 0, nullable environment metadata and authoritative conversation/run/revision checks. The native vault-bound broker independently binds summary identity to the observed tenant/project and binds Changes responses to that summary conversation plus requested run, scope, turn and revision; it uses the real summary endpoint without inventing a generic Cloud run-detail preflight. UI context replacement and refresh cancellation suppress stale summary, snapshot, reference and loading updates. These authority and lifecycle changes do not supply missing clean aggregate or native execution evidence and retain the existing partial status and Cloud Kasm cookie limitation. The shared Workbench capability snapshot now uses a required V2 snapshot authority instead of App assembling its business dependencies through a static provider. The provider freezes configuration and forwards snapshot reads with an AbortSignal; the outer operation captures current generation actions once and obtains a parent service lease. Child capability reads derive leases from that admitted parent generation, including during generation replacement, and reject attempts to acquire children after release. The dependency factory constructs the existing business operation ports within this boundary. Branch settlement and operation tracking drain admitted reads before parent release, so an early failure or cancellation cannot leave successful sibling reads outside the snapshot lifetime. The UI ignores cancelled late success as well as late failure and performs no reads while disabled. These shared composition and lifecycle sources are recorded centrally here; they do not change individual business capability availability, observed authority provenance, existing partial aggregate requirements or the separate Cloud Kasm native cookie limitation. The snapshot journey dependency uses the existing Cloud request broker with same-origin and cancellation checks; construction failures are observed by the snapshot branch and never select a legacy fallback. App republishes the snapshot client when host generation actions change, so an initially unavailable generation is retried when ready and HMR aborts the previous UI request while retaining same-generation client stability.
